## Why this matters

A shared set of tools means anyone in the lab can find, open and continue anyone else's work. This module is mostly hands-on: by the end, your accounts are set up and connected. All of these tools have excellent tutorials; if you don't know one, follow the link, create an account and watch the intro video.

## Everything lives in the cloud [BA]{.ba-tag}

::: callout-important
## Super important
We **don't use local files**, such as an Excel sheet saved on one specific computer. Everything is in the cloud, in Google Workspace, so it is shared, backed up and version controlled.
:::

- [Google Workspace](https://workspace.google.com/) tools: Docs, Drive, Sheets, Forms, Calendar, Meet. They make collaboration easy.
- [OSF](https://osf.io/) keeps *all* files of a research project together, and is where we publish data and materials.
- Always use [headings](https://support.google.com/docs/answer/6367684) and [reference management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reference_management_software) in manuscripts. Module 5 covers both in detail.

## Communication and scheduling [BA]{.ba-tag}

- We communicate on [Slack]({{< var links.slack >}}). Rarely, when outside parties are involved, we use MS Teams.
- Meetings and task deadlines are scheduled in [Google Calendar](https://calendar.google.com/).
- Meetings are online in [Google Meet](https://meet.google.com/) by default.
- For finding a time for group meetings we often use [Doodle](https://doodle.com/). Link it to your Google Calendar so it can see when you are busy.
- For external communication, the lab has a shared email address: {{< var links.lab_email >}}.

## Project management in ClickUp

We use [ClickUp]({{< var links.clickup >}}) to track tasks, who is responsible, dependencies and deadlines.

- Team members share progress and comments on the task itself.
- Task outputs (documents, repositories) are linked from the task, so others can find them.
- It shows bottlenecks early and makes it easier to share or reallocate work.

Your own onboarding is a ClickUp task, too. Each **Do** item in this course is a subtask there.

## At the university [BA]{.ba-tag}

- Set up [eduroam](https://www.esnelte.hu/wifi-setup-elte) for internet access on campus.
- University software licences are available from the [ELTE IIG site](https://iig.elte.hu/content/szoftver-disztribucio.cl.991?m=5807).

## Reference manager [BA]{.ba-tag}

You **must** use a reference manager; handmade reference lists are not acceptable. Our primary one is [Paperpile](https://paperpile.com/), because it works reliably both in Google Docs and in offline word processors, but it isn't free. Two free options are [Zotero](https://www.zotero.org/) and [Mendeley](https://www.mendeley.com/). If you don't have a Paperpile licence, use Zotero with its Google Docs integration.

## Do

These tasks are also in your ClickUp onboarding task.

- [ ] Accept the ClickUp invitation and find your onboarding task.
- [ ] Send your Google account address to the lab leader so you can be added to shared folders and calendars.
- [ ] Create an [OSF](https://osf.io/) account and send your profile link to the lab leader.
- [ ] Connect Doodle to your Google Calendar.
- [ ] Set up eduroam on your laptop and phone.
- [ ] Install Zotero (or Paperpile) and connect it to Google Docs. Test it: insert one citation and a bibliography into a new Google Doc.

## Check yourself

::: quiz
You collected pilot data in an Excel file on the lab computer. What should you do with it?

- [ ] Leave it there; everyone in the lab can use that computer.
- [ ] Email it to yourself so you have a copy.
- [x] Move it to the project's shared cloud folder (Google Sheets or the project's Drive/OSF folder).

::: explain
We don't use local files. Data and documents go to the shared cloud storage of the project, where they are backed up, version controlled and accessible to the team.
:::
:::

::: quiz
Which reference list is acceptable in a lab manuscript?

- [ ] A carefully typed APA reference list.
- [ ] References copied from Google Scholar's "Cite" button.
- [x] A bibliography generated by Paperpile, Zotero or Mendeley.

::: explain
Handmade reference lists aren't accepted, however careful. A reference manager keeps citations and the bibliography consistent and lets us switch citation style with one click.
:::
:::

::: quiz
Where do you check whether a task assigned to you has a deadline and who else is working on it?

- [ ] Slack
- [x] ClickUp
- [ ] Google Drive

::: explain
ClickUp tracks tasks, responsible people, dependencies and deadlines. Slack is for conversation, not for tracking.
:::
:::
